full_caption: Ulric Umberton, Appellant, v. Perrin Nettleford, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Ulric Umberton, as servicer for the holder of the note, commenced this foreclosure against Perrin Nettleford with respect to the property at 180 Pennyroyal Court, Grayrock, WM, securing an original principal balance of $320,000.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The allonge produced at trial was undated and was not physically affixed to the note when the original was tendered for inspection. An allonge must be affixed to the instrument to be effective as an endorsement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: A servicer that accepts payments under a trial plan and then denies permanent modification without the review the plan promises may be estopped from asserting the default those payments were tendered to cure.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The statute of limitations on a foreclosure action runs from acceleration, not from the original maturity date. Where an earlier acceleration was withdrawn by dismissal of a prior action, the limitations clock is reset as to installments coming due thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Post-sale, the purchaser takes subject to any bona fide tenancy of record. A tenant in possession under a lease predating the mortgage is not divested by the sale.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Standing to foreclose requires that the plaintiff hold the note, endorsed in blank or to the plaintiff, at the time the complaint is filed. A later-acquired endorsement does not cure a standing defect existing at filing.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Strict compliance with contractual notice conditions is a condition precedent to acceleration. The notice sent to Perrin Nettleford omitted the reinstatement advisory and was therefore ineffective to accelerate the debt.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: A deficiency judgment is available only where the foreclosure sale price is confirmed as commercially reasonable. The bid of $90,000 against an appraised value of $340,000 is presumptively unreasonable and requires an evidentiary hearing.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Perrin Nettleford made 5 payments under a trial loan-modification plan and was thereafter denied a permanent modification on the ground of an unverified escrow shortfall of $3,700.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The judgment of foreclosure is vacated and the cause remanded with directions to dismiss without prejudice for failure to satisfy the notice condition precedent.

sections.heading: RIDER B — LOSS MITIGATION AND TRIAL PLAN
sections.text: Upon receipt of a complete loss-mitigation application more than 21 days before a scheduled sale, Servicer shall evaluate the application for all available alternatives to foreclosure and shall not move for judgment or conduct a sale while the evaluation is pending. Where Borrower makes all payments required by a trial plan, Servicer shall offer a permanent modification on the terms the trial plan describes, and may not deny the modification on a ground that was known and could have been raised before the trial plan was offered.

sections.heading: RIDER C — ESCROW ACCOUNT
sections.text: Borrower shall pay monthly into escrow one-twelfth of the annual taxes and insurance premiums. Servicer shall conduct an annual escrow analysis and shall furnish Borrower a statement identifying any shortage or surplus. A shortage of $3,700 or less shall be spread over not fewer than twelve monthly installments and shall not, standing alone, constitute a default.

sections.heading: RIDER E — TENANT PROTECTIONS AFTER SALE
sections.text: A purchaser at the sale takes subject to any bona fide tenancy in existence at the time of the notice of sale. The purchaser shall give a bona fide tenant not less than 45 days' written notice to vacate, and a tenant under a bona fide lease may occupy the Property for the remaining term of the lease unless the purchaser will occupy the Property as a primary residence.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 15 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Grayrock County, Westmarch, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 15 days of recording.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.
